scope_note: Provisional two-pass discovery, adversarial correction and gap-closure account for Meta's multi-building Fort Worth data-center campus and the selected 634,395-square-foot IM3 footprint. The current Tarrant Appraisal District address search resolves exactly three accounts at 4500 Like Way and none at 5000 Like Way: Winner real 42324937, Winner personal 14401610 and separately owned MMI Southwest personal 14628223. Campus evidence remains unallocated because no public crosswalk maps the inventory footprint to Building 3, Building 4.2, Building 5-6, FTW4 or assessor substructures. QTS's separately operated physical campus at 14100 Park Vista remains excluded, while Meta personal-property account 14780998 at that address is retained as an explicit company-county boundary exception. Account values, jurisdiction-specific exemptions, taxes paid through two collectors, audit actuals, permit projections, overlapping cumulative totals, grants and infrastructure payments remain separate. County, construction and supplier models remain rejected, while policy-authorized arithmetic tax aggregations, a cost break-even identity, a 2018 gross-before-abatement counterfactual, an operating-payroll sensitivity and 2024 electricity benchmark, average-load and location-based emissions syntheses are retained separately as modeled—not observed or audited—results.

project_updates.title: Identity, boundary and chronology
project_updates.notes: Meta broke ground in 2015 and reports the Fort Worth campus operational since 2017; continuous construction and TDLR phases extend the chronology through the 2022 FTW4 schedule and a 2023 small retrofit search result. The current assessor address inventory resolves three accounts at 4500 Like Way and zero at 5000, but no source crosswalks the campus to the selected inventory building.
project_updates.project_description: Meta Fort Worth is Meta’s multi-building data-center campus at 4500 Like Way in north Fort Worth, Tarrant County, operated through Winner LLC. Winner broke ground in 2015 and the campus began operating in 2017; public audit and permit records trace later buildings, utilities and retrofit phases through 2023. The selected IM3 object is one 634,395-square-foot mapped footprint, but public records do not crosswalk it to Meta’s Building 3, 4.2, 5-6 or FTW4 identifiers, so campus totals remain unallocated. QTS’s physical campus at 14100 Park Vista remains excluded, while Meta-owned assessed equipment there is disclosed separately.

project_updates.title: Winner LLC operator crosswalk
project_updates.notes: SEC subsidiary exhibits list Winner LLC under Meta, while TDLR, Fort Worth audit, appraisal and tax-abatement sources connect Winner to 4500 Like Way and the Facebook/Meta project. Company-wide SEC financials were searched but contain no Fort Worth investment, revenue, payroll, tax, utility or community allocation.

project_updates.title: Adjacent QTS boundary exclusion
project_updates.notes: Tarrant agreement, permit, appraisal, operator and archive searches found Winner's proposed 2019 retrofit at 14100 Park Vista, while current QTS material identifies that address as QTS FTW1. TAD now directly identifies Meta personal-property account 14780998 there and links it to Winner real account 42324937, so its 2021-2025 equipment assessments are retained as a company-county boundary exception. No deed or operating crosswalk transfers QTS's physical facility to Meta; QTS power, area and cooling figures remain excluded.

project_updates.title: Assessor, tax roll and bill search
project_updates.notes: Corrected by account-level evidence below. The 2024 top-taxpayer roll remains a distinct City-tax-unit aggregate and is not added to account series. Exact Like Way searches, three TAD accounts, three Tarrant collector accounts and three matching Denton collector ...TAR accounts now establish annual values, jurisdiction-specific exemption treatment, paid levies, dates, payers, zero balances and six recipient distributions.

project_updates.title: City incentives, compliance and payments search
project_updates.notes: Fort Worth CSC 46728, CSC 46727, amendments, audit reports, council packets, contracts, check register and FY2025 accounts-payable audit were reopened. The PeopleSoft audit confirms $14,415,465.40 paid to Winner LLC during October 2023-August 2024 with no exception, but it omits voucher, check, invoice, fund, account, purpose and contract coding. The linked FY2024 detail workbook returned HTTP 403/Akamai Access Denied through direct and browser routes. Because neither the amount nor a component is linked to Chapter 380 or tax abatement in the available record, it remains an unresolved AP aggregate rather than an incentive record.

project_updates.title: County incentive and abatement search
project_updates.notes: Tarrant agreements and schedules establish a conditional ten-year County 60% / Hospital 40% abatement structure; the existing 2018 realized County $1,476,619.34 and Hospital $944,148.72 records remain the only published tax-savings dollars. Account portals now separately show Tarrant-serviced Contract Abatement assessment exemptions for Winner real and personal property from 2018-2025 and no Northwest ISD exemption. Those exemption bases are documented in each assessment record but are not multiplied by generic rates into savings.

project_updates.title: State incentive, exemption and financing search
project_updates.notes: Texas Comptroller records confirm Winner LLC d/b/a Ernst LLC certification from June 22, 2015 through June 22, 2035, establishing eligibility for the qualified-data-center sales/use-tax exemption. Certificate and state transparency routes disclose no annual or cumulative tax-exempt purchase amount or realized state revenue reduction for this campus; no value is imputed from purchases, investment or statewide totals. No TEF, Chapter 313, public-bond or TIF amount was found.

project_updates.title: Planning, permit and phase search
project_updates.notes: Fort Worth issued-permit reports, development portal, Certificates of Occupancy references, TDLR TABS and archived construction reporting were searched by Winner, Project Ernst, FTW, address, lot and contractor. Four major TDLR estimated-cost observations are retained as source projections without summation; local permits also show later electrical, fire-water and retrofit work but no complete non-overlapping permit ledger or IM3 crosswalk.

project_updates.title: Construction workforce and payroll search
project_updates.notes: Operator, DPR/Fortis contractor, audit, permit, council, workforce-board, QCEW and archive sources were reopened. A mechanical $784,208,681 / 1,200 peak-worker ratio and a 9.46% Fort Worth-spend share were tested and rejected: peak concurrent workers are not job-years or a payroll denominator, construction covers 2015-2017, local spend mixes labor and materials, and phase hours, wages, residence and equipment exclusions are absent. No multiplier satisfies the named-model, vintage, geography and channel-separation requirements.

project_updates.title: Supplier and local-spend search
project_updates.notes: Audit invoices, pay applications, vendor-address verification, contractor announcements, procurement, M/WBE, council and vendor-payment routes were reopened. The audited $74,215,330 is address-verified Fort Worth construction spend, not a supplier-payroll base. Supplier/induced candidates using that amount were tested and rejected because industry split, margins, imports, ownership, worker residence, annual timing and a named local input-output model are absent. No complete supplier or operating-purchase ledger was found.

project_updates.title: Operations employment and payroll search
project_updates.notes: Meta careers, operator posts, incentive agreements, audit compliance, QCEW, CBP, workforce and archive sources were reopened. The greater-than-150 December 2020 people snapshot now supports a low-confidence annual-payroll sensitivity using exactly 150 people and same-vintage Dallas-Fort Worth BLS occupation benchmarks; it is explicitly a conservative scenario anchor, not observed payroll, current headcount, a true-value bound or local household income. The conditional 200-plus jobs-supported projection remains excluded because it may include multiplier channels. Benefits, payroll taxes, bonuses, equity, overtime, contractor margin, occupation mix, hours, residence and retention remain unresolved; induced-employment candidates still fail named-multiplier and double-counting gates.

project_updates.title: Electric utility and grid search
project_updates.notes: Meta energy reports, PUC service-area directories, ERCOT, Oncor, Brazos, AllianceTexas, tariff, substation and council sources were reopened. Multiplying the exact 2020-2024 kWh series by retail-commercial, utility-average or energy-only tariffs was tested and rejected: provider, voltage, rate class, coincident demand, load factor, power factor, riders, taxes, negotiated supply and demand charges are unresolved. The sensitivity would model an arbitrary bill, not campus electricity economics.

project_updates.title: Water, wastewater and reclaimed-water search
project_updates.notes: Fort Worth utility agreements, council records, water and wastewater rates, TWDB, TCEQ, Meta water reports and restoration-benefit reports were searched. The 2.45 MGD agreement figure is capacity, not use; Meta directly reports 2020-2024 withdrawals of 300, 254, 346, 404 and 311 megaliters, but the locked catalog lacks an actual-withdrawal metric, so the series is documented rather than mislabeled as planned use. No consumption, discharge, reclaimed-water volume, bill or selected-building allocation was found.

project_updates.title: Environmental and generator search
project_updates.notes: TCEQ air application, permit, emission-event, stormwater and compliance routes plus EPA ECHO and operator environmental reports were searched for Alliance Site, Winner, Meta and 4500 Like Way. Location-based and market-based scope 2 values are outside the locked catalog, and no stable generator count, fuel use, operating hours, actual criteria emissions, discharge or violation amount was retained.

project_updates.title: Community recipient confirmation search
project_updates.notes: Operator grant lists, school, museum, Nature Center, nonprofit, city budget, council and local-news archives were searched. Three museum grants are recipient-confirmed and retained inside the non-additive $5.2 million-plus county-area total; a $300,000 Nature Center commitment and other named recipients lacked equally clear payment evidence or complete annual coverage and were not inserted.

project_updates.title: Infrastructure and public-service cost search

project_updates.title: County GDP, employment and wage model dispositions
project_updates.notes: Actual governed-panel diagnostics used both plausible events: 2015 groundbreaking and 2017 operation, eight pre-years, complete 2001-2024 outcomes, study-county exclusion, counties at 0.35-2.5x Tarrant population, log-growth pretrend RMSE and equal-weight nearest donors. For 2015 national five-donor matches, pretrend RMSE / pre-2020 gap / 2022-2024 gap were employment 1.46% / -2.16% / +2.94%, wage 0.76% / -1.59% / -2.36%, GDP 1.62% / +1.98% / +10.44%; donor sets were respectively Queens/Oklahoma/Wake/Suffolk/Essex, Orange CA/Alameda/Duval/Dallas/Norfolk, and Honolulu/Westchester/Worcester/Harris/Franklin. For 2017, results were employment 0.90% / +1.01% / +5.68%, wage 0.80% / +0.58% / +1.01%, GDP 1.13% / +0.62% / +8.72%. K=3/5/10 and Texas-only sensitivity reverses or materially shifts results: 2015 recovery employment -2.47% to +7.58%, GDP -6.22% to +13.47%; 2017 recovery employment +2.29% to +8.64%, GDP -3.56% to +9.90%. Pandemic 2020-2021 was isolated rather than pooled. Continuous phases, donor data-center contamination, population/industry differences and result instability fail comparison-design and attribution gates. All three county gaps remain missing; no mechanical gap is published as a Meta effect.
